Here are some open source reddit bots that you could probably use as a basis.

As well, just ask Google how to build a bot, their are a million tutorials that make it very simple.

I would also suggest that you ask the admins what the conditions are for running a bot on this site as other similar sites have conditions they impose on known bots.

I would recommend waiting for the major Voat API update before putting any serious work into a bot.

In the simplest terms:

  • You will need to work in a programming language, not HTML/CSS.

  • Your program will need to run on your local machine or a server that you own, 24/7, to watch for new posts or comments periodically and then react accordingly by sending requests via the API.

Reddit bots are a good start for learning from, although most will not directly translate to Voat without some serious tinkering. Many Reddit bots are written with PRAW as mentioned by Ar_Nimruzir, which is a wrapper that simplifies some common Reddit API functions, and is written in Python.

You can use anything from Python, Perl, PHP, Java, JavaScript (probably Node.js), Ruby… almost all programming languages will have libraries for interfacing with the web.

Murder wasn't just legal, it was big business.

At the end of the first age of the twenty first century, If you made it onto Inter-Tech’s public list of criminally wanted men, anyone who carried an operating license could find you and they could kill you. These private contractors didn’t have to worry about prosecution or collateral damage because along with their license, each contractor was protected by a one billion dollar insurance policy compliments of the international licensing consortium and a written promise to get you out of any legal trouble, as long as you abided by the terms of service that you agreed to when you were issued your license

Inter-Tech piloted the contract killer program in the UK with just ten names at any given time. For months no one made a move. But eventually, as trust grew in the bounties paid by the company one of the contracts reported as claimed. The first was followed by another. Then two more within a week of each other. By the fall of twenty one-twenty five, the list had grown to include thousands of names and completed contracts were reported every hour. Even when listed criminals fled to countries that didn’t recognize Inter-Tech or the consortium, no contract world wide lasted longer than seven days.

“Do you see him?” asked Elijah Welch.

“Nope, not yet,” said Isaac Cardenas. “The man downstairs told me he was having dinner down the street like he does every tuesday night. We’ll give him another couple of hours.”

“And then?”

Isaac looked away from the window, “And then-- We'll see.”

Elijah used binoculars to look across the street at the dark empty apartment. Isaac just watched with ice blue eyes.

“Or you know. Maybe. Maybe-maybe-maybe,” said Elijah. “Maybe he’s made us. Maybe he knows we’re here. He could even be sending a couple of guys--”

“Made us?”

“You know. Found us out. Know’s were here. Made us!”

Isaac shook his head at looked at the younger man with a half smile. “Look,” he said. “I don’t mind teaching you the ropes kid, but can you not talk like that? This isn’t some old time movie, it’s work. We are employees of Inter-Tech doing a job like any other job. As much as you want it to be, this isn’t exciting. As much as you hope it is, it’s not going to be an adventure.”

“Sorry. I just--”

“Don’t worry about it. You just keep your eyes on that apartment,” said Isaac. “I’ll worry about the rest.”

Isaac and Elijah were set up safely in a hotel room across the street from where the contract had been renting a room. It had cost the two contract killers almost two hundred dollars for a room across the street and another hundred for the overnight clerk to not ask for ID, but if they completed this contract, they’d get almost a hundred times that amount. Inter-Tech paid well in this economy. That meant job security, but it also meant a lot of competition.

The contract request had come in an hour before via Inter-Tech’s contract app. Elijah wasn't licensed yet and it would be at least a month until his background check came through so it would have to be Isaac who finished all the jobs. Until Elijah could learn to fly on his own, Isaac had agreed to take him on as an apprentice.

“So how long have you been doing this?” asked Elijah.

“About a year.” he said. “Had me my bag, would ya?”

“How did you get into it?”

Elijah went over to the nightstand and grabbed Isaac's bag and brought it over to him. He took off his gloves and reached into the bag finding a sandwich and a couple of cans of pop. His hand’s weren’t human, they were mechanical. Dark steel with blue and chrome colored bits of plastics connected with black rubber joints.

“I used to work over at Caldwell soups. I did landscaping for thirty years. Do you know what they used to pay me to mow their lawns?”

Elijah looked up from Isaac’s hands and shook his head.

“Two hundred grand a year. Full benefits. A nice retirement. Then the governor decided that the state needed three more international star ports to stay competitive. Raised business taxes. Came in one day and they told me, 'Sorry pal, no more lawns for you.' Just like that.” Isaac unwrapped the sandwich and took a bite from one of the quarters. “You want half?” he asked.

Elijah’s eye were still fixed on Isaac’s hands. Isaac just sighed and took another bite of his ham and cheese.

“Let me guess,” he said. “You’ve never seen prosthetic hands either.”

Elijah shook his head.

“Are you sure you're right for this job? You seem kind of sheltered, kid.”

“I’m not,” said Elijah. “I mean, I am. But I’m not. I mean--”

“Look, I don’t care,” he said. “It was just an observation. Every man has a right to his own path. You should just make sure that this is the path for you. But about the hands--Before you ask, I’ll tell you. I lost my hands in a car accident. No, I can’t feel anything. That model is too expensive and I lost my benefits. Yes, these work fine. No, I don’t jerk off anymore. Any other questions?”

“Yeah,” said Elijah finally looking up from the prosthetics. “What’s it like to kill somebody? I mean, does it bother you?”

Isaac opened up one of the cans and drank half of it burping into a robotic fist.

“It’s like driving a bus. It’s like delivering a package. It’s like--It’s like mowing a lawn. Killing somebody is just like earning a paycheck,” he said.

Across the street, the lights of the room came on and the contract came into view. Elijah picked up his binoculars and saw the man for the first time.

“Quick,” said Isaac, ”Confirm the target.”

“Huh?”

“Confirm the target! Confirm the target! Use the App!”

“Oh!”

Elijah grabbed the tablet and opened the app. After a welcome screen, options appeared. Elijah chose the option to request an authorization.

Please verify the target, read the app.

Elijah picked up the binoculars and looked into the room. The display of the binoculars had changed and he could see an infrared view of the hotel room. The contract’s body pulsed as it walked around and a green square appeared over the man’s face and another over his heart.. The display then froze to a single image and text appeared on the tablet reading, analyzing data...

Elijah put down the binoculars and picked up the tablet.

‘Contract confirmed. Authorization number 789543897 for this contract is issued. The authorization number will expire in 9 minutes.’

“Got it,” said Elijah.

Isaac reached into the bag and pulled out an old style Mosin Nagant Sniper Rifle and looked across the street into the room. The rifle had no scope but Isaac seemed to be tracking the man as he walked around the apartment though he couldn’t be seen through the window yet.

“Aren’t you gonna use--”

“Don’t talk.” said Isaac.

Elijah wordlessly picked up the tablet and requested more information about the contract.

“Isaac,” said Elijah. “Two other authorizations have also been issued on the contract! Somebody else is going after-”

“Shit,” said Isaac. For an instant, the contract came into view. It was just enough time for Isaac to pull the trigger. The bullet left a small hole in the window of both rooms and the contract dropped immediately. “Now! Verify the kill now!”

Elijah held up the binoculars again. As he did the front door of the contract’s hotel room door burst open. Someone ran in holding a tablet of their own and held it over the rapidly cooling body.

Analyzing... read the app.

“Come on,” said Isaac. “Come on, god damn it.”

A second man walked into the room holding a machete. He stared at the Isaac and Elijah through the hotel window. Issac just smiled and gave a lazy wave.

“We got it yet?” asked Isaac.

“No! Not yet!”

Contract confirmed, read the app. Payment has been requested. Thank you for using Inter-Tech. Would you like to leave a review of this contract?

In the far room, the man holding the tablet angrily raised it over his head and smashed it down onto the ground.

“Not bad for a guy with prosthetics, huh?” said Isaac. “Now let’s get the hell out of here.”

The two packed everything up and were in the hallway and down the elevator before the hotel clerk could look up from his ledger.

Their car was parked three blocks over and two blocks up. Isaac walked briskly but never under stress. Elijah on the other hand kept looking over his shoulder.

“What did you mean,” said Elijah. “About the prosthetics?”

“You're kidding, right?”

“No.”

“I didn’t just lose my hands, kid. I lost my eyes too. And my ear. And my left foot. Had prosthetics put in all over. Now my hands I regret losing, but my eyes? I can see better then you can with those binoculars.”

The two put their supplies in the back of Isaac's truck and got in.

“So could you make out what those guys looked like across the street. I mean like really make them out?” asked Elijah, “ Did you know them?”

“Know them? No. But I could tell you the color of their eyes.” he said.

Payment complete, The app displayed brightly in the dark cab of the truck.

Isaac looked at it then at Elijah.

“Where to now?” he said.

The app immediately lit up with a brightly colored prompt. Would you like to accept a new request? Surge Pricing is currently in effect.

That's a false dichotomy. All kinds of trials have gotten to the point of requiring far more time and expence than they should. It's pretty obvious the guy was guilty, so why drag it out for years? Another example is that James Holmes guy. These are open and shut cases, regardless of the sentence.

Of course a fair trial is crucial. Is there any evidence that he didn't get a fair chance to defend himself, or that he needed two whole years to build a case?

The reason that "open and shut" cases like this get lengthy trials is that we don't want to leave room for loopholes to extend the process any further. When we're absolutely sure that someone is guilty of a heinous crime, we don't offer them a plea bargain deal for a lighter sentence in lieu of court. Considering we were pushing for the death penalty and actually got it, that is by nature going to be a long trial. When someone's life hangs in the balance, it deserves more than a cursory "Yep, he did it, let's hang him." because that's just not who we are as a people. As has become evident in the recent CNN "Mortal Kombat murders" coverage on the Charleston killings and the recent string of media articles, it's clear that in addition to somehow spinning a "games have finally grown up, therefore GG and gamers are dead" angle, the narratives aren't even pretending to mask the self-righteous megaphoning just under the surface. Not to mention the thinly-veiled revenge seeking that also drive such narratives more and more. And it's not just limited to gaming.

Take the approach the same CNN coverage used on Southerners for instance. I'm not from the South. But one doesn't have to be some stereotypical Bible-thumping redneck to realize how much the slander and shaming, the efforts to paint things like Southern Pride or the notion of the South as hate crimes have less to do with "social justice," "fighting slavery and racism," or some other platitude. Rather it seems from this part of the globe, it's more like a spiteful effort to put an final end to the American Civil War by ensuing that Southerners are shamed and patronized into oblivion.

Still, what are your thoughts, KiA?
